pr_metadata.title: feat: Add “align” parameter for ui.inline #1535
pr_metadata.description:
This PR adds a new `align` parameter to `ui.inline` that allows users to specify the vertical alignment of the items.

The API is updated as follows:

```diff
 interface Inline {
   /** The components laid out inline. */
   items: Component[]
   /** Specifies how to lay out the individual components. Defaults to 'start'. */
   justify?: 'start' | 'end' | 'center' | 'between' | 'around'
+  /** Specifies how the individual components are aligned on the vertical axis. Defaults to 'center'. */
+  align?: 'start' | 'end' | 'center' | 'baseline' | 'stretch'
   /** Whether to display the components inset from the parent form, with a contrasting background. */
   inset?: B
 }
```

The PR also adds a new example showing how values for the `justify` and `align` parameters of `ui.inline` work:
<video src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7029582/205581533-c932cbdb-a2ae-4265-a4d2-8fcc076bbdcb.mov">

I also renamed the `alignment` parameter of the internal function `XComponents` to `justify` (more details here: 08d6813fe66bc1b316f00d93010e40095fb26331).

Closes #1535.

gold_comments.issue_summary:
Since `all_*` lists are hardcoded, you can be sure that `q.args` value, if specified, is within the list. You can further simplify:

```suggestion
    justify_current = q.args.justify if q.args.justify else 'start'
    align_current = q.args.align if q.args.align else 'center'
```
gold_comments.evidence_requirement: The added line `align_current = q.args.align if q.args.align in all_align else 'center'` (line 16) uses an unnecessary membership check against a hardcoded list.
gold_comments.rationale: Since `all_align` is a hardcoded list and the choice_group only offers values from that list, the membership check is redundant and the code can be simplified as suggested by the reviewer.
